expectations.text: Names the custom VQL dialect as the anti-pattern, since a language not already widely supported makes every BI-tool integration start from zero
expectations.evidence: "a custom dialect where a standard wire protocol was available."

expectations.text: Recommends speaking an existing wire protocol, specifically a Postgres wire-protocol endpoint, as the cheapest connectivity rung, because every BI tool, psql, and every ORM already ships a Postgres driver
expectations.evidence: "use a standard wire protocol... Tableau and Power BI use their existing PostgreSQL connectors, with no `.taco`, no certification cycle".

expectations.text: States the cost of the wire-protocol rung: commitment to the Postgres dialect and its type system, and nothing exotic
expectations.evidence: Says customers write ClickHouse SQL; the Postgres-dialect commitment is not stated as a cost.

expectations.text: Rejects the 'a sprint or two and then it's done' scoping and frames BI-tool support as an ongoing certification tax budgeted as continuing engineering rather than a one-time integration
expectations.evidence: "A driver is a recurring cost, not a one-off build."

expectations.text: Requires accurate SQLSTATEs if a driver is shipped, specifically SQLSTATE 28000 for invalid credentials, warning that a generic error instead can break Tableau connector behavior
expectations.evidence: "Returning a generic error instead of 28000 for bad credentials can break connector behavior."

expectations.text: Names signed per-tool connector packages whose signing certificates expire and must be renewed on a schedule
expectations.evidence: "signed `.taco`. An expired signing certificate makes Tableau reject it outright."

expectations.text: States that Power BI certification requires documented customer demand via a public ideas-forum thread and submission by pull request to Microsoft's connector repository
expectations.evidence: "documented customer demand (a public ideas-forum thread). You submit by pull request to Microsoft's connector repository."

expectations.text: States that certification transfers distribution but not support, with first-line connectivity issues routed back to the data-source owner
expectations.evidence: "Microsoft distributes the connector but routes customer issues back to you."

expectations.text: Rejects admitting arbitrary customer SQL onto the shared production ClickHouse cluster, naming the blast radius across the whole application
expectations.evidence: "customer SQL admitted onto the shared production cluster" is a named failure mode; PostHog "basically untenable"; worst-case query threatens the product.

expectations.text: Recommends single-tenant or per-organization engine instances fronted by one wire-protocol endpoint as the fix for the isolation and connectivity problems at once
expectations.evidence: PostHog "rebuilt on per-organization engine instances behind a Postgres wire-protocol endpoint"; per-tenant compute isolation named as target state.

expectations.text: Names engine drift as a distinct risk: a query engine changing results between releases or depending on enabled settings, which a vendor's own regression suite never covers across arbitrary customer query shapes
expectations.evidence: "Engine drift is a documented risk. PostHog saw ClickHouse change results between releases, and your test suite can't cover every customer query shape."

expectations.text: Requires a connection-setup page per supported client covering the URL template, the driver class or download, the auth method, and TLS stated as an explicit requirement rather than left to client defaults
expectations.evidence: Says "Publish a connection-setup page per tool" and "Enforce TLS" separately, without specifying the page contents.
